claims.head: The Senators feed on mistakes, and the Islanders make them
claims.call: The Senators get at least their usual 7.6% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
claims.body: The Senators turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Islanders are one of the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Islanders.
claims.nums: Ottawa 9th for chances off turnovers (7.6% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · NY Islanders 31st for avoiding breakdowns
claims.gist: The Senators pounce on loose pucks, and the Islanders cough them up.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 expected goals within 5 seconds of winning the puck
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Depth against star power
claims.body: On depth, the Islanders is the league’s best and Ottawa is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.gist: The Islanders and the Senators sit at opposite ends for depth.
claims.call: The Islanders spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Senators.

check.rule: held if the team comes out ahead by at least half its usual margin; partly if it comes out ahead by less; otherwise didn't happen

notes.text: M. Barzal is day to day and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters. V. Eklund has taken his spot beside B. Schenn and C. Ritchie.
K. Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 37% last season.
A. Zub has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman.
J. Sanderson is out and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
J. Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 41% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, up from 4% last season.

OTT.head: Ottawa should have the upper hand
OTT.body: Ottawa has controlled the play far better over recent games, the Islanders may be without Barzal, and Ottawa has home ice. The Islanders can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

NYI.head: A tough matchup for the Islanders
NYI.body: Ottawa has controlled the play far better over recent games, the Islanders may be without Barzal, and Ottawa has home ice. The Islanders’ best way through is keeping shots to a minimum.
